about: Concrete comparison cases (spec section 6). Each case fixes a goal, its inputs and admissible hypotheses, a target, a metric with its direction, and the applicable results. The viewer calculates every guarantee from the named formula and the inputs (src/model.js, CASE_FORMULAS); tests/test_cases.py recalculates them independently. The formulas are the standard statements of the cited results. These are calculated guarantees, not published empirical measurements. A result that does not apply is excluded from the rank, with its reason. The judge (claude-opus-5-5) authored the cases; the dates are judge-supplied citations of the original publications, not retrieved from a declared source.

cases.title: Upper tail of a sum of independent fair coin flips
cases.question: How small an upper bound on P(S ≥ 60) does each result give, where S is the number of heads in 100 independent fair coin flips?
input_text: n = 100 independent Bernoulli(p) variables X_1, ..., X_n, each in [0, 1]
p = 0.5, so E[S] = np = 50 and Var(S) = np(1 - p) = 25
deviation t = 10: the event is S ≥ np + t = 60
hypotheses: the distribution of each X_i is known (Bernoulli(p))
cases.target: an upper bound on P(S ≥ np + t) for this fixed n (not a limit)

reference.label: exact binomial tail (a check value, not a result)

entries.requires: S ≥ 0 and E[S] finite: holds here

date.basis: no documented original publication in the declared sources

entries.requires: finite variance: holds here; the two-sided bound also bounds the upper tail

date.basis: P. Chebyshev, Des valeurs moyennes, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2) 12 (1867) 177-184 (judge-supplied citation)

entries.tex: P(S \ge np + t) \le \inf_{s>0} e^{-s(np+t)}\,\mathbb{E}[e^{sS}] = e^{-n\,D(p + t/n \,\|\, p)}
entries.requires: the moment generating function of S: known here, because each X_i is Bernoulli(p)

date.basis: H. Chernoff, Ann. Math. Statist. 23(4) (1952) 493-507, doi:10.1214/aoms/1177729330 (judge-supplied citation)

entries.requires: independence and X_i in [0, 1]: holds here; the distribution is not needed

date.basis: W. Hoeffding, J. Amer. Statist. Assoc. 58(301) (1963) 13-30, doi:10.1080/01621459.1963.10500830 (judge-supplied citation)

entries.requires: martingale differences X_i - p with |X_i - p| ≤ c: holds here; independence is not needed

date.basis: K. Azuma, Tohoku Math. J. 19(3) (1967) 357-367, doi:10.2748/tmj/1178243286 (judge-supplied citation)

entries.excluded: The central limit theorem gives a limit as n tends to infinity. It gives no bound for the fixed n = 100, so it has no value for this metric.

cases.title: Existence of a satisfying assignment: union bound against the local lemma
cases.question: Does each result prove that a 10-CNF formula with 10000 clauses, where each clause shares variables with at most 300 other clauses, has a satisfying assignment?
input_text: k = 10 distinct variables in each clause; a uniform random assignment makes a clause false with probability 2^-k
m = 10000 clauses (bad events A_j: clause j is false)
d = 300: each clause shares a variable with at most d other clauses, so each A_j is independent of all but at most d others
hypotheses: a dependency graph of maximum degree d
cases.target: P(no bad event occurs) > 0, which proves that a satisfying assignment exists

metric.name: the sufficient condition of the result, evaluated on the inputs
metric.unit: condition value (the result proves existence when it is below its threshold)

entries.requires: only the probabilities of the bad events; no dependency information

date.basis: G. Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854) (judge-supplied citation)

entries.requires: a dependency graph of maximum degree d: holds here

date.basis: P. Erdős and L. Lovász, Problems and results on 3-chromatic hypergraphs and some related questions, in Infinite and Finite Sets (1975) (judge-supplied citation)

cases.title: Probability of a union of three events
cases.question: What upper bound on P(A ∪ B ∪ C) does each result give from the stated probabilities?
hypotheses: the intersection probabilities are known (inclusion-exclusion only)
cases.target: an upper bound on P(A ∪ B ∪ C)

entries.tex: P(A \cup B \cup C) \le P(A) + P(B) + P(C)

date.basis: G. Boole, An Investigation of the Laws of Thought (1854) (judge-supplied citation)

entries.tex: P(A \cup B \cup C) = \sum P(A) - \sum P(A \cap B) + P(A \cap B \cap C)

date.basis: no documented original publication in the declared sources

cases.title: Euler characteristic of a closed surface from its curvature
cases.question: Which results give the Euler characteristic of a closed oriented surface of genus 2 from a metric of constant curvature -1?
input_text: a closed oriented surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of constant Gaussian curvature K = -1
its area is 4π (from the hyperbolic metric)
hypotheses: a compact Riemannian manifold without boundary
cases.target: the value of the Euler characteristic χ

entries.requires: a compact 2-dimensional Riemannian manifold without boundary

date.basis: no documented original publication in the declared sources

entries.requires: a compact even-dimensional Riemannian manifold without boundary; here n = 1

date.basis: no documented original publication in the declared sources

entries.requires: an elliptic operator on a closed manifold; here d + d* from even to odd forms, whose index is χ

date.basis: no documented original publication in the declared sources

cases.note: All three results give the same value. No result dominates on this metric; the trade-off is the machinery that each one needs (see the proof simplicity and effort columns, which are judgments).
